cover letter
01. Please describe how you have supported diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility in your work, and how you anticipate continuing to support these principles in this role.
Applicable District, local, State and federal policies, laws and regulations related to areas of assignment. Basic principles and practices of purchasing.
Analyze problems, identify alternative solutions, project consequences of proposed actions and implement recommendations.
Basic principles of risk management, including safety hazards and appropriate precautions applicable to area of assignment.
Collect, compile and analyze data.
Budget preparation and administration.
Encourage professional excellence among the staff and promote an organizational culture of customer service, innovation, and quality services.
Correct English composition, grammar, spelling and vocabulary. District and College organization, operations and objectives.
Establish and maintain cooperative working relationships with those contacted in the course of work. Evaluate needs and estimate future supply requirements for supplies and other inventory items.

Effective methods, practices and procedures used in a District-wide warehouse operation involving the receipt, storage, distribution, delivery, inventory and issuance of supplies, equipment, materials and miscellaneous items.
Interpret, apply and explain complex and technical local, State and federal policies, laws, regulations and other legal mandates related to areas of assignment.
Equipment and materials used in warehouse operations including familiarity with computerized warehouse or inventory application programs.
Maintain accurate records and controls.
Operation of computer, peripherals and software programs, including database management, spreadsheet, word processing and specialized software.
Manage a District-wide warehouse operation for the successful receipt, issuance, distribution, delivery, storage and inventory of supplies, equipment, materials and miscellaneous items.
Principles and procedures of record keeping. Principles of training and supervision.
Meet schedules and timelines.
Observe health and safety rules and regulations.
Perform assigned work with speed and accuracy.
Prepare and administer budgets for assigned program areas.
Prepare and maintain a variety of warehouse-related records and reports.
Relate effectively to people of varied academic, cultural and socioeconomic background using tact, diplomacy and courtesy.
Select and recommend the purchase of routinely used materials and supplies. Train, supervise and evaluate the performance of assigned personnel.
Understand and effectively and collaboratively work in a complicated multi-college environment, as well as within a system of community college districts.
Work effectively with others to achieve common goals including student recruitment and retention. Work independently with minimum supervision.
WORK ENVIRONMENT AND PHYSICAL DEMANDS

The conditions herein are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential job functions.
Work Environment:

The work assigned to this classification is typically performed in a warehouse environment. While performing the duties of this classification, the employee regularly works in extreme heat and cold conditions and is regularly exposed to fumes, airborne particles, toxic or caustic chemicals. Safety shoes and protective clothing are required. The work environment is noisy. Enlist at least minimal environmental controls to assure health and comfort.
Physical Demands:

Incumbents regularly required to stand and walk on hard surfaces for extended periods of time; use hands to finger, handle, or feel objects, a keyboard or other office machines, tools or controls; reach with hands and arms; bend, stoop, kneel or crouch; speak clearly and distinctly to provide information; and hear and understand voices over telephone and in person; maneuver effectively in confined spaces. Employees assigned to this classification must regularly lift, carry and/or move objects weighing up to 75 pounds.
Interpersonal skills including tact, patience and diplomacy. Inventory control.
Communicate clearly, concisely and effectively, both orally and in writing, with diverse constituencies within and outside of the District.
Oral and written communication skills. Planning and organizational skills.
Maintain current knowledge of bidding procedures and purchasing operations. Maintain inventory control of warehouse supplies and equipment.
Operate a variety of equipment including a small truck, forklift, pallet jack and hand truck.
Operate office equipment such as computer, printer, calculator, copier and facsimile machine. Organize time and workspace effectively.
